text: 9.4.1 Introduction
trace: 9.3 M-Plane operational state --> 9.4.1 Introduction

text: This clause defines an optional O-RU capability which allows O-RU Controllers to configure the O-RU to provide notifications of modifications to its YANG datastore. This capability can be used when the O-RU is operating in a hybrid environment with multiple simultaneous NETCONF sessions established to different O-RU controllers. Using this capability, one particular O-RU controller uses the NETCONF notifications functionality as specified in RFC 6470 \[35\] to enable it to be automatically signalled changes to the O-RU's configuration made by a second O-RU controller. Additionally, if the O-RU supports a vendor specific interface to allow manual configuration, this functionality can also be used to signal such configuration modifications to an O-RU Controller.
trace: 9.3 M-Plane operational state --> 9.4.1 Introduction

text: 9.4.2 Subscribing to updates from an O-RU
trace: 9.3 M-Plane operational state --> 9.4.2 Subscribing to updates from an O-RU

text: 10.1 General
trace: 10 Performance management --> 10.1 General

text: This clause provides the description of scenarios related to performance management. It consists of 2 functions. One is for the measurement activation and the other is the collection of measurement results.
trace: 10 Performance management --> 10.1 General

text: Performance management key concepts:
trace: 10 Performance management --> 10.1 General

text: Measurement group: A group of measurement objects that belong to the same category, e.g. tx-stats. Each measurement-group is associated with a measurement-group identifier that is used in file management processing \(See clause 10.3.2\)
trace: 10 Performance management --> 10.1 General

text: Measurement object: Object on which performance is measured, e.g. RX\_POWER, TX\_POWER. Only when combined with a report-info, it defines a metric.
trace: 10 Performance management --> 10.1 General

text: Object unit: Granularity to measure the performance per measurement object, e.g. PORT\_NUMBER, EAXC\_ID.
trace: 10 Performance management --> 10.1 General

text: Report info: Type of the measurement, e.g. MAXIMUM, MINIMUM. Only when combined with a measurementobject, it defines a metric.

text: 10.2 Measurement configuration, activation and de-activation
trace: 10 Performance management --> 10.2 Measurement configuration, activation and de-activation

text: The measurement activation at the start-up installation is described in clause 6.
trace: 10 Performance management --> 10.2 Measurement configuration, activation and de-activation

text: This clause provides information about how to configure, activate and de-activate the performance measurement in an O-RU. The performance measurement schema nodes are defined in o-ran-performance-management YANG module. In case of multiple NETCONF clients, only one NETCONF client shall activate/deactivate the measurements in the O-RU. The O-RU shall support those measurements described as mandatory in clause 9.1 of the O-RAN CUS plane specification \[2\].
trace: 10 Performance management --> 10.2 Measurement configuration, activation and de-activation

text:
* NOTE 1: The naming convention of schema nodes that report capability for each measurement-group \(in container measurement-capabilities\) uses an abbreviated form of the measurement-group name \(enough to uniquely identify the measurement-group\), ending with "-objects". e.g. transceiver-objects, rx-windowobjects.
  * NOTE 2: The naming convention of schema nodes that are used to configure each measurement-group uses an abbreviated form of the measurement-group name \(enough to uniquely identify the measurement-group\), ending with "-measurement-objects". e.g. transceiver-measurement-objects, rx-windowmeasurement-objects.
  * NOTE 3: The naming convention for schema node \(list\) to define notification content of each measurement-group \(as part of notification measurement-result-stats\) uses measurement-group name, for example, ethernet-stats, tx-output-power-stats, etc.
trace: 10 Performance management --> 10.2 Measurement configuration, activation and de-activation

text: The detail of the measurement-group\(s\), including measurement-object\(s\), object-unit\(s\) and report-info\(s\) supported by M-Plane are defined in clause Annex B.
trace: 10 Performance management --> 10.2 Measurement configuration, activation and de-activation

text: For each measurement-group, at least one of the capabilities may be reported: supported measurement-object\(s\), supported report-info\(s\) per measurement-object and supported object-unit\(s\) per measurement-object.
trace: 10 Performance management --> 10.2 Measurement configuration, activation and de-activation

text: For each active measurement, the NETCONF client shall configure measurement-interval per measurement-group using respective measurement-interval parameter. It defines performance measurement periodicity, e.g. 300, 600, 900 seconds. measurement-objects belong to a measurement-group inherit the measurement-group measurementinterval.
trace: 10 Performance management --> 10.2 Measurement configuration, activation and de-activation

text: NETCONF client can configure a measurement-group with measurement-objects belonging to it. For each measurement-object, object-unit and report-info\(s\) are configured. For selected report-info, the NETCONF Client may configure additional parameters, e.g. function, bin-count, upper-bound, lower-bound.
trace: 10 Performance management --> 10.2 Measurement configuration, activation and de-activation

text: Measurement shall be activated using parameter active per measurement-object when report-info\(s\) and measurement-interval for the measurement-object is/are configured. A measurement-object can be activated and deactivated at any time.
trace: 10 Performance management --> 10.2 Measurement configuration, activation and de-activation

text:
* When different measurement-group\(s\) have intervals with a common factor, the O-RU shall synchronise the boundary of these intervals with this factor, irrespective of when the different measurement-objects are activated, as illustrated in Figure 10.2-1. All of start points of the measurement-intervals of measurementgroups shall be synchronised to zero o'clock mid-night by using an equation \{full seconds \(hour, minute and second\) modulo 'measurement-interval' = 0\}, in order to ensure the same start and end of the measurementintervals between O-RUs. For more details see the following illustration.
  * The start-time and end-time indicate the time of measurement start and end for the measurement-object at each measurement-interval.

Removal of measurement-object\(s\) from a measurement-group configurations \(by configuring schema nodes, e.g. transceiver-measurement-objects, rxwindow-measurement-objects, etc.\) shall be allowed only when active for those intended to be removed measurement-object\(s\) has value FALSE.

text: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result

text: 10.3.0 Introduction
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.0 Introduction

text: This clause provides the description of scenarios used to collect measurement results. There are three options:
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.0 Introduction

text:
* 1\) NETCONF process: Create-subscription from NETCONF client and NETCONF notification from NETCONF server are used.
  * 2\) File Management process: File upload mechanism is used to transfer the measurement file from O-RU to configured file server\(s\) that O-RU can reach to.
  * 3\) Configured subscription process: Create configured subscription from O-RU as Event-Producer to Event-Collector.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.0 Introduction

text: Methods 1 and 2 are mandatory for the O-RU. Method 3 shall be supported by those O-RUs that support the optional NON-PERSISTENT-MPLANE feature. The method\(s\) to be used is the matter of NETCONF client.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.0 Introduction

text: In case of multiple NETCONF clients and/or Event-Collectors, the O-RU shall report the same notification-based measurement results to all subscribed NETCONF clients/Event-Collectors, and the O-RU shall upload file-based results to all configured fileservers.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.0 Introduction

text: 10.3.1 NETCONF process for dynamic subscriptions
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.1 NETCONF process for dynamic subscriptions

text: This process needs the NETCONF capability: urn:ietf:params:netconf:capability:notification:1.0.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.1 NETCONF process for dynamic subscriptions

text:
* 1\) NETCONF client subscribes to one or more measurement group\(s\) and/or measurement-object\(s\) to collect the measurement result by sending NETCONF <create-subscription> to NETCONF server in the O-RU. In this message, startTime and stopTime for the notification may be configurable. NETCONF client can configure the notification-interval in the performance-management YANG module.
  * 2\) NETCONF server sends NETCONF notification messages periodically to the client as configured by the notification-interval. The NETCONF notification message contains subscribed measurement group\(s\) and/or measurement-object\(s\). The notification-interval does not need to be same as the measurement-interval. The notification timing different from the measurement-interval is a matter to O-RU implementation.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.1 NETCONF process for dynamic subscriptions

text: This procedure is described in Figure 10.3.1-1.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.1 NETCONF process for dynamic subscriptions

text: Figure 10.3.1-1: NETCONF process of Measurement Result Collection
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.1 NETCONF process for dynamic subscriptions --> Figure 10.3.1-1: NETCONF process of Measurement Result Collection

text: A NETCONF client may use the create-subscription for the single event-stream "measurement-result-stats", or alternatively subscribe the default event-stream using additional filter criteria to identify those measurements of interest to the client. In order to subscribe multiple notifications, the appropriate create-subscription message is required. Refer to clause 11.3 for the appropriate example of create-subscription of multiple notifications.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.1 NETCONF process for dynamic subscriptions

text: In order to terminate the subscription, the NETCONF client shall send <close-session> operation from the subscription session or configuring the <stopTime> parameter when the subscription was created. If NETCONF session is terminated by <kill-session>, the subscribed notification is terminated as well.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.1 NETCONF process for dynamic subscriptions

text: When notification-interval is larger than measurement-interval, O-RUs implementing v07.00 or later of the present document may use a single notification that contains multiple stats included in the list such as multiple-transceivermeasurement-result, multiple-rx-window-measurement-result, multiple-tx-measurement-result, multiple-epemeasurement-result or multiple-symbol-rssi-measurement-result which have consecutive periods indicating starttime and end-time for the measurement.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.1 NETCONF process for dynamic subscriptions

text:
* NOTE 2: When multiple measurements stats corresponding to the same measurement-group are available in an O-RU that implements an earlier version of the present document, the O-RU is only able to include a single statistic in the notification. In such circumstances, the O-RU should report the latest available statistic in the notification.
  * NOTE 3: An O-RU Controller that implements an earlier version of the present document can ensure that the configuration of notification-interval and measurement-interval results in only a single measurement statistic corresponding to a specific measurement-group being reported by the O-RU in any one notification. In other cases, the O-RU Controller can use the rules defined in clause 4.3 to ignore the newly introduced schema-nodes for reporting multiple measurements.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.1 NETCONF process for dynamic subscriptions

text: When notification-interval is smaller than measurement-interval, one notification may not contain the stats which start-time and end-time are not applicable to the period for the notification.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.1 NETCONF process for dynamic subscriptions

text: For example, when notification-interval = 60min, measurement-interval for measurement-object\#A= 30min and measurement-interval for measurement-object\#B = 15min, one notification contains 2 measurement results for measurement-object\#A with consecutive start-time and end-time, and 4 measurement results for measurementobject\#B with consecutive start-time and end-time.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.1 NETCONF process for dynamic subscriptions

text: For the other example, when notification-interval = 15min, measurement-interval for measurement-object\#A= 30min and measurement-interval for measurement-object\#B = 15min, one notification contains one measurement results for measurement-object\#B but not for measurement-object\#A. next notification contains both measurements result for measurement-object\#A and \#B.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.1 NETCONF process for dynamic subscriptions

text: 10.3.2 File management process
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.2 File management process

text: NETCONF client needs to configure a parameter of performance measurement YANG module 'enable-file-upload' to enable or disable the periodic file upload mechanism via NETCONF <edit-config>. Its default is FALSE.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.2 File management process

text: In addition, the performance measurement YANG module defines file-upload-interval, remote-file-upload-path, credentials information of the file server and enable-random-file-upload as configurable parameters.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.2 File management process

10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.2 File management process

text: Following types of authentications shall be supported for performance file upload:
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.2 File management process

text: a\) Password for RU authentication and list of public keys \(see clause 5.4 in the present document\) for sFTP server authentication.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.2 File management process

text: Following types of authentications may be supported for performance file upload:
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.2 File management process

text:
* b\) X.509 Certificate for FTPES client \(O-RU\) and FTPES server.
  * c\) Certificate for both O-RU and sFTP server authentication.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.2 File management process

text: When the parameter enable-file-upload is set to TRUE, O-RU shall store the performance measurement files in the generic folder in O-RU, i.e. O-RAN/PM/ or o-ran/pm/. Every file-upload-interval, O-RU pushes the latest file to upload to the remote-file-upload-path of the configured SFTP/FTPES servers if enable-file-upload is set to TRUE. Otherwise, the performance measurement file is not created and uploaded. The O-RU shall use the URI scheme of the remote-file-path leaf to determine whether to use sFTP or FTPES for the file upload. The number of maximum performance files to be stored in O-RU simultaneously is a matter for O-RU implementation. The O-RU shall manage its own storage space by deleting the older files autonomously. An O-RU Controller shall only trigger file upload using FTPES if it is using NETCONF/TLS to configure the O-RU.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.2 File management process

text: The O-RU shall ensure that the start-time and the end-time within the name of the performance measurement file are synchronised with the same manner as measurement-interval by using file-upload-interval.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.2 File management process

text: If the parameter enable-random-file-upload is set to TRUE, the O-RU shall randomize the timing to upload SFTP or FTPES file after the performance measurement file is ready to upload. The randomized timing is an O-RU implementation matter and shall not be later than next file-upload-interval.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.2 File management process

text: The file name of the performance measurement is:
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.2 File management process

text: C<start-time>\_<end-time>\_<name>.csv
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.2 File management process

* Starting with a capital letter "C".
  * Format of <start-time> and <end-time> can be local time or UTC.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.2 File management process

text: Local time format is YYYYMMDDHHMM+HHMM, indicating, year, month, day, hour, minute, timezone "+" or "-" , hour and minute for the time zone.
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.2 File management process

text: UTC format is YYYYMMDDHHMMZ, indicating, year, month, day, hour, minute and with a special UTC designator \("Z"\)
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.2 File management process

text: Time zone offset is provided by timezone-utc-offset in o-ran-operation.yang.

text:
* <name> in ietf-hardware is used.
  * "\_" underscore is located between <start-time>, <end-time> and <name>.
  * File extension is "csv" as csv format file.

text: The file format of the performance measurement has following rule:
trace: 10.3 Collection and reporting of measurement result --> 10.3.2 File management process

text:
* 1\) Each line starts with an identifier. The identifier should be used to identify each measurement-group defined by its row in Table B.1-1, e.g. transceiver-stats should be identified by an identifier of "1", rx-window-stats should be identified by a measurement-group identifier of "2" and tx-measurement-objects should be identified by a measurement-group of "3", etc.
  * NOTE 1: The use of the identifier to identify a measurement group is only recommended in order to accommodate an earlier release of the present document where the use of the identifier was ambiguous.
  * 2\) After the measurement-object identifier, the name of measurement-object, start-time, end-time are appended.

text:
* 3\) Then the object-unit and object-unit-id are appended, followed by the set of report-info are repeated in one line.
  * NOTE 2: If the leading identifier is not used to signal a measurement-group, the measurement-group needs to be derived from the object-unit. For example, an object-unit of "PORT\_NUMBER" is used to identify the transceiver-stats measurement-group, and an object-unit of "ianahw:port" is used to identify an epe-stats measurement group for the ianahw:port hardware class.
  * NOTE 3: If a measurement is referenced by multiple object-units, each object-unit and corresponding objectunit-id are appended in turn.
  * 4\) When the YANG definition of the measurement-result-grouping includes one or more lists and multiple report-info parameters exist per object-unit, all of the report-info are consecutively listed until the next object-unit-id. The order of parameters, such as object-unit-id, report-info and additional information for the report-info, shall be same as the order of those listed in NETCONF notification defined in o-ran-performancemanagement YANG module.
  * 5\) When the YANG definition of the measurement-result-grouping includes one or more containers, the container name is included in the report-info.
  * NOTE 4: In versions prior v13.0 of the present document, the use of the container name in the report-info was not defined and hence how such measurement reports were encoded was not specified.

text: 11 Fault management
trace: 11 Fault management

text: 11.1 Introduction
trace: 11 Fault management --> 11.1 Introduction

text: Fault management is used to manage active-alarm-list and optionally historical-alarm-list; handle alarm subscription and send alarm notifications to subscribers, which will typically be the NETCONF Client unless the O-RU supports the configured subscription capability, as described in clause 18, when the configured subscriber may be an Event-Collector.
trace: 11 Fault management --> 11.1 Introduction

text: The NETCONF Server shall manage the active-alarm-list. Alarms with fault-severity set to WARNING are excluded from this list. When the raise alarm criteria are met, an alarm is raised and it is added to the list; when clear alarm conditions are fulfilled then the alarm is cleared and removed from the active-alarm-list. Furthermore, when the element that was the fault-source of an alarm is deleted then all related alarms are removed from the active-alarm-list.
trace: 11 Fault management --> 11.1 Introduction

text: Optionally, the NETCONF Server is also responsible for managing the historical-alarm-list. Alarms with fault-severity  set to WARNING are excluded from this list. When an alarm is cleared, it is added to this list with is-cleared set to "true".
trace: 11 Fault management --> 11.1 Introduction

text: The NETCONF Client can read " active-alarm-list" by get RPC operation, as illustrated in Figure 11.1-1.
trace: 11 Fault management --> 11.1 Introduction

text: Figure 11.1-1: Read Active Alarms
trace: 11 Fault management --> 11.1 Introduction --> Figure 11.1-1: Read Active Alarms

trace: 11 Fault management --> 11.2 Alarm notification

trace: 11 Fault management --> 11.2 Alarm notification

text:
* a new alarm is added to active-alarm-list;
  * an alarm is removed from the list.

This applies to alarms which were explicitly related to the deleted "fault-source" element. The rationale for such is to avoid misalignment between NETCONF Clients when one NETCONF Client deletes an element.
trace: 11 Fault management --> 11.2 Alarm notification

text: 11.3 Manage alarm subscription to NETCONF clients
trace: 11.3 Manage alarm subscription to NETCONF clients

     xmlns="urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:netconf:notification:1.0">

     <severity>critical</severity>
     </event>
     <event xmlns="http://example.com/event/1.0">
     <eventClass>fault</eventClass>
     <severity>major</severity>
     </event>
     <event xmlns="http://example.com/event/1.0">
     <eventClass>fault</eventClass>
     <severity>minor</severity>
     </event>
     </filter>
     </create-subscription>

text: 11.4 Fault sources
trace: 11.3 Manage alarm subscription to NETCONF clients --> 11.4 Fault sources

text: Alarm notifications reported by NETCONF Server contain element "fault-source" which indicates the origin of an alarm. In general values of "fault-source" are derived from names defined as YANG leafs:
trace: 11.3 Manage alarm subscription to NETCONF clients --> 11.4 Fault sources

text:
* Source \(Examples: fan, module, PA, port\) indicates that origin of the alarm within the O-RU. Value of "fault-source" is derived from element name.
  * Source \(other than when an element is within the O-RU\)
trace: 11.3 Manage alarm subscription to NETCONF clients --> 11.4 Fault sources

text: Value of fault-source may identify the O-RU external resource; for example, antenna line.
trace: 11.3 Manage alarm subscription to NETCONF clients --> 11.4 Fault sources

text: Alarm instance can be identified by value combination of fault-id, fault-source and fault-severity. Alarms with different "fault-id", "fault-source" or "fault-severity" are independent:
trace: 11.3 Manage alarm subscription to NETCONF clients --> 11.4 Fault sources

text:
* Multiple alarms with same "fault-id" may be reported with different "fault-source".
  * Multiple alarms with same "fault-source" may be reported with different "fault-id".
  * Among alarms with same value of fault-id and fault-source and different value of fault-severity, only one of them can be in the active-alarm-list at a given time. When an alarm with a "fault-id" and a "fault-source" is reported with a "fault-severity", and there is already an alarm in the active-alarm-list with same fault-id, fault-source value, but with a different fault-severity, NETCONF server shall simultaneously add the alarm with new fault-severity in active-alarm-list and clear the previous alarm with different fault-severity by setting is-cleared to TRUE and shall remove the alarm with previous fault-severity from the active-alarmlist. NETCONF server shall notify subscribers of added and removed alarms.
trace: 11.3 Manage alarm subscription to NETCONF clients --> 11.4 Fault sources

text: The range of "fault-id" is separated to common and vendor specific. The common fault-ids are defined in clause A and more numbers may be used in future. The vendor specific range for the fault-id shall be \[1000 .. 65535\].
trace: 11.3 Manage alarm subscription to NETCONF clients --> 11.4 Fault sources

text: Alarm notifications reported by the NETCONF Server contain names of the "affected-objects" which indicate elements affected by the fault. In case the origin of the alarm is within the O-RU, other elements than "fault-source" which do not
trace: 11.3 Manage alarm subscription to NETCONF clients --> 11.4 Fault sources
11.3 Manage alarm subscription to NETCONF clients --> 11.4 Fault sources
11.3 Manage alarm subscription to NETCONF clients --> 11.4 Fault sources
11.3 Manage alarm subscription to NETCONF clients --> 11.4 Fault sources
11.3 Manage alarm subscription to NETCONF clients --> 11.4 Fault sources

text: function correctly due to the fault are reported via "affected-objects". In case the origin of the fault is outside of the O-RU, the O-RU elements which do not function correctly due to the fault are reported via "affected-objects".
trace: 11.3 Manage alarm subscription to NETCONF clients --> 11.4 Fault sources

text: 12.3 File management operation: upload
trace: 12.2 File system structure --> 12.3 File management operation: upload

text: This clause describes file upload method from O-RU to the fileserver. sFTP or FTPES is used for File management, and one file can be uploaded by one upload operation. The O-RU Controller triggers file upload operation to O-RU.
trace: 12.2 File system structure --> 12.3 File management operation: upload

text: Simultaneous multiple file upload operations can be supported under the same FTP connection between O-RU to the fileserver. If the O-RU has a limitation with regard to the ability to upload files simultaneously, it is allowed that O-RU reports failure notification for the simultaneous upload request which exceeds its capability. The behaviour of O-RU Controller is out of scope when O-RU Controller receives failure notification from the O-RU.
trace: 12.2 File system structure --> 12.3 File management operation: upload

text: Following rpc is used for upload operation.
trace: 12.2 File system structure --> 12.3 File management operation: upload

text:
* rpc: file-upload 
    * input 
      * local-logical-file-path: the logical path of file to be uploaded \(no wildcard is allowed\)
      * remote-file-path: URI of file on the fileserver
      * credentials: authentication credentials for file server access
      * application-layer-credential: application layer level authentication credentials for file server access
    * output 
      * status: whether O-RU accepted or rejected the upload request
      * reject-reason: the human readable reason why O-RU rejects the request \(only applicable if status is rejected\)
trace: 12.2 File system structure --> 12.3 File management operation: upload

text: In the rpc-reply, status whether the O-RU receives the upload request or rejects due to some reason \(e.g. the number of limitation to upload simultaneously\) is replied. If rejected, the human readable reject reason is also replied.
trace: 12.2 File system structure --> 12.3 File management operation: upload

text: In notification, the result of the upload process \(successfully uploaded or failed upload\) is replied in addition to locallogical-file-path and remote-file-path. If failure, the human readable reason is also replied. Figure 12.3-1 shows the file upload sequence diagram.

text: This clause describes the file download method from O-RU Controller to O-RU. sFTP or FTPES is used for File management, and one file can be downloaded by one download operation. O-RU Controller triggers the file download operation to O-RU.

text: Simultaneous multiple file download operations can be supported under the same FTP connection between the O-RU and O-DU/SMO. If the O-RU has the number of limitation to download simultaneously as a capability, it is allowed that the O-RU reports a failure notification for the download request which is larger than the capability. text: 13 Synchronisation aspects
trace: 13 Synchronisation aspects

text: 13.1 Introduction
trace: 13 Synchronisation aspects --> 13.1 Introduction

text: This clause describes the YANG model \(o-ran-sync.yang\) containers that are used for the Management Plane's interactions with various aspects of the time synchronisation of the O-RU. In general, the O-RU shall manage its synchronisation status and select one or more synchronisation input source\(s\) \(based on vendor specific implementation\). Additional information regarding the interactions between M-Plane and S-Plane are described in the current specification's clause 15.3.3 and in the CUS-Plane specification \[2\], clause 11.4.
trace: 13 Synchronisation aspects --> 13.1 Introduction

text: The o-ran-sync.yang YANG model defines configuration, status and notification containers which are used to enable O-RU controller to recover the state of the O-RU's S-Plane. Before going into the details of each of these an overview of these objects is provided here.
trace: 13 Synchronisation aspects --> 13.1 Introduction

text: The YANG model defines several configuration containers. These containers comprise read/write parameters that can be read or set by the O-RU controller. The O-RU controller can read them \(to determine O-RU configuration\) or set them \(to change the O-RU's configuration\). These are:
trace: 13 Synchronisation aspects --> 13.1 Introduction

text:
* PTP Configuration ptp-config: O-RU controller can set or read PTP parameters like PTP Full/Partial timing support profiles, accepted clock classes, and set network address among other parameters
  * PLFS/SyncE Configuration synce-config: This container provides SyncE information such as the acceptable list of SSMs.
  * GNSS \(Global Network Satellite System\) Configuration gnss-config: This container comprises leaves which define whether GNNS can be used, and if so which satellite constellation to use.
  * Sync Capability sync-capability: This is a read-only container indicates to the O-RU controller the time accuracy of the T-TSC or T-BC that is integrated into the O-RU.
trace: 13 Synchronisation aspects --> 13.1 Introduction

text: The O-RU should store the above synchronisation configuration in reset persistent memory.
trace: 13 Synchronisation aspects --> 13.1 Introduction
13 Synchronisation aspects --> 13.1 Introduction
13 Synchronisation aspects --> 13.1 Introduction
13 Synchronisation aspects --> 13.1 Introduction
13 Synchronisation aspects --> 13.1 Introduction

text: During the start -up installation process \(see clause 6.1\) the O-RU's default startup configuration settings may allow the O-RU's S-Plane to become operational without any configuration by the O-RU controller. The O-RU uses its default configuration settings to execute the PTP and/or PLFS/SyncE protocols, or GNSS settings to complete the synchronisation process \(including optional features such as PER-PORT-PTP-CONFIG, PER-PORT-SYNCE-CONFIG, GNSS, ANTI-JAM\). During the start-up installation flow the startup settings may be changed. This may be necessary if the default synchronisation settings are incompatible with the network implementation. If the startup configuration requires changes, the O-RU controller first retrieves the synchronisation configuration and status from O-RU, and then the O-RU controller modifies the configuration. The O-RU shall then execute the synchronisation process using the updated settings. Having these settings stored in reset persistent memory typically simplifies subsequent startup flows by enabling O-RU to start up without reconfiguration.
trace: 13 Synchronisation aspects --> 13.1 Introduction

text: Once the O-RU is operational, the O-RU controller can subscribe to several synchronisation notifications which report to the O-RU controller the status of the O-RU. The following notifications are defined in the YANG model.
trace: 13 Synchronisation aspects --> 13.1 Introduction

text:
* synchronization-state-change conveys the sync-state.
  * ptp-state-change conveys the ptp-status.
  * synce-state-change If SyncE or another PLFS is used, this conveys the synce-status
  * gnss-state-change If a O-RU supports GNSS capability, this conveys the gnss-status.
trace: 13 Synchronisation aspects --> 13.1 Introduction

text: During normal operation, the O-DU should monitor the operational state of the O-RU's S-Plane. This is accomplished by subscribing to receive the synchronization-state-change notification. If the O-DU is notified that the O-RU's state has changed to UNLOCKED, the O-DU shall stop sending data to the O-RU and shall ignore any data from that O-RU. Clause 15.3.3 describes in more detail the interactions between S-Plane and M-Plane when synchronisation is lost and when synchronisation is recovered.
trace: 13 Synchronisation aspects --> 13.1 Introduction

text: NOTE: Except for possible configuration during the start-up installation process, the synchronisation start-up and reference clock selection are accomplished via S-Plane protocols independent of M-Plane.
trace: 13 Synchronisation aspects --> 13.1 Introduction

text: The remainder of this clause describes in more detail the main objects within the configuration, status, and notification containers. However, this clause does not describe all of the leafs/objects within the containers. Some items for example time-error, frequency-error, supported-reference-types are not mentioned in this clause, but are defined and described in o-ran-sync.yang.
trace: 13 Synchronisation aspects --> 13.1 Introduction

text: 13.2 Sync status object
trace: 13.2 Sync status object

text: This sync-state container provides synchronisation state of the module. If the O-RU Controller is interested in receiving Synchronization status state information, it may configure a subscription to the synchronization-state-change notification from the O-RU. Event notifications will be sent whenever the state of the O-RU synchronisation changes.
trace: 13.2 Sync status object

text: For an O-DU that is communicating with an O-RU, the synchronization-state-change notification is the primary mechanism by which the O-DU knows whether the O-RU is synchronised and is ready to transmit/receive when fully configured. This notification is the primary mechanism to transfer status information required to implement the flows described in clause 15.3.3.
trace: 13.2 Sync status object

text: The state diagram of O-RU synchronisation is shown in Figure 13.2-1, and is indicated by the following allowed values:
trace: 13.2 Sync status object

text:
* LOCKED: O-RU is in the locked mode, as defined in Recommendation ITU-T G.810 \[23\].
  * HOLDOVER: O-RU clock is in holdover mode.
  * FREERUN: O-RU clock is not locked to an input reference and is not in the holdover mode.

trace: 13.2 Sync status object

trace: 13.2 Sync status object

text:
* GNSS

text: 13.3 Sync capability object
trace: 13.3 Sync capability object

text: The module's synchronisation capability is provided via the sync-t-tsc object. This object indicates the accuracy of the O-RU's derived Telecom Subordinate Clock \(T-TSC\). For details on the actual capability levels, see clause 11.3 of the O-RAN WG4 CUS plane specification \[2\]. There are two enumerations possible:
trace: 13.3 Sync capability object

text:
* CLASS\_B: Regular accuracy \(previously referred to class B\) for synchronisation is supported by the device as per IEEE 802.1CM \[80\] clause 6.4.1, Case 1.1.
  * ENHANCED: Enhanced accuracy for synchronisation is supported by the device as per IEEE802.1CM \[80\] clause 6.4.1, Case 1.2.

trace: 13.3 Sync capability object

* a Boolean called boundary-clock-supported, which indicates whether the O-RU supports T-BC profiles defined in ITU-T 8275.1 \[22\].
  * a Boolean called extended-ql-tlv-supported, which indicates whether the O-RU supports the extended Quality Level TLV defined in ITU-T 8264 \[76\] clause 11.3.

text: 13.4.1 Introduction
trace: 13.3 Sync capability object --> 13.4.1 Introduction

text: The ptp-config container contains information about the O-RU's configuration of Precision Time Protocol. This clause describes the definitions of the items contained within ptp-config.
trace: 13.3 Sync capability object --> 13.4.1 Introduction

text: domain-number: This parameter indicates the Domain Number for PTP announce messages. Allowed values: 0 ~ 255.
trace: 13.3 Sync capability object --> 13.4.1 Introduction

text: • Recommendation ITU-T G.8275.1 \[22\] uses domain numbers in the range 24...43, but the entire range is allowed to ensure flexibility of the M-Plane specification. For Recommendation ITU-T G.8275.2 domain numbers from range 44…63 shall be used.
trace: 13.3 Sync capability object --> 13.4.1 Introduction

text: default: 24.
trace: 13.3 Sync capability object --> 13.4.1 Introduction

text: accepted-clock-classes: Contains the list of PTP acceptable Clock Classes, sorted in the descending order.
trace: 13.3 Sync capability object --> 13.4.1 Introduction
13.3 Sync capability object --> 13.4.1 Introduction

text: default: 7, 6
trace: 13.3 Sync capability object --> 13.4.1 Introduction

text: clock-classes: The PTP Clock Class accepted by the O-RU. Allowed values: 0 ~ 255.
trace: 13.3 Sync capability object --> 13.4.1 Introduction

text: • Not all values are compliant to \[22\], but the entire range is allowed in M-plane specification to ensure flexibility. The values can be validated/filtered on the receiver side, if necessary.
trace: 13.3 Sync capability object --> 13.4.1 Introduction

text: ptp-profile: Defines which PTP profile will be used.
trace: 13.3 Sync capability object --> 13.4.1 Introduction

text: Allowed values:
trace: 13.3 Sync capability object --> 13.4.1 Introduction

text:
* G\_8275\_1 \(multicast over Ethernet will be used, see Recommendation ITU-T G.8275.1 \[22\]\)
  * G\_8275\_2 \(unicast over IP will be used, see Recommendation ITU-T G.8275.2\)
trace: 13.3 Sync capability object --> 13.4.1 Introduction

text: default: G\_8275\_1.
trace: 13.3 Sync capability object --> 13.4.1 Introduction

text: delay-asymmetry: Defines the static phase error in the recovered PTP timing signal to be compensated at the O-RU. The error is defined in units of nanoseconds in the range ±10 000 ns. This is a single global value that is common for all the O-RU's ports. As specified in Recommendation ITU-T G.810 \[23\] and IEEE1588 \[24\] and \[50\], the sign of the parameter shall be interpreted as follows:
trace: 13.3 Sync capability object --> 13.4.1 Introduction

text:
* If the phase error to be compensated is negative, then the recovered timing signal shall be advanced by the time interval equal to the configured value to compensate the error.
  * If the phase error to be compensated is positive, then the recovered timing signal shall be delayed by the time interval equal to the configured value to compensate the error.
trace: 13.3 Sync capability object --> 13.4.1 Introduction

text: default: 0

trace: 13.3 Sync capability object --> 13.4.2 G.8275.1 specific parameters

Before requesting or subscribing to SyncE status information, the O-RU Controller shall ensure that SyncE is supported at the O-RU by requesting the supported timing reference types, as defined earlier in clause 13.2. The following list summarizes the related parameters of this container.

text: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling

text: 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling

text: This clause clarifies Supervision Failure Handling and Supervision Termination Handling.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling

text: When Supervision Failure is detected by O-RU, the O-RU shall immediately disable operation of the watchdog timers for the corresponding NETCONF session. O-RU assumes NETCONF session related to failed supervision is no longer valid. O-RU shall terminate this invalid NETCONF session by closing underlying SSH or TLS connection. Then O-RU shall start performing the call home procedure towards the NETCONF client, using the re-call-home-no-ssh-timer to repeat the call home attempts. This activity is repeated by the O-RU until, either:
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling

text: 1\) A new NETCONF session is established with the original NETCONF client.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling

text: Or,
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling
14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling
14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling
14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling
14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling

text: 2\) the original NETCONF client is no longer a "call home O-RU Controller" as defined in clause 6.3, e.g. when reperforming DHCP configuration, the O-RU Controller identity corresponding to the NETCONF client is no longer signalled by the DHCP server, and/or the NETCONF client was previously configured using the configured-client-info container and this configuration has been deleted.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling

text: Or,
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling

text: 3\) After max-call-home-attempts has been reached and a new NETCONF session cannot be established with the original NETCONF client.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling

text: Scenario 2 and 3 result in one of the two described cases:
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling

text: Case \#1: The O-RU is still having at least one running and valid NETCONF session with a NETCONF client that has subscribed to receive the supervision-notification and where the per-odu-monitoring container is not present in the O-RU's configuration.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling

text: The O-RU remains operational and stops performing call home to this O-RU controller.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling

text: Case \#2: The O-RU does not have running NETCONF session with any NETCONF client that has subscribed to receive the supervision-notification.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling

text: The O-RU ceases all radio transmission and performs autonomous reset.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling

text: When an O-RU indicates it supports the SHARED-ORU-MULTI-ODU feature, an O-RU Controller can enable supervision operation on a per O-DU identity basis by configuring one or more odu-id parameters in the per-odumonitoring container in o-ran-supervision YANG model. When an odu-id has been configured in the per-odumonitoring container, the O-RU shall enable operation of watchdog supervision timers \(supervision timer and notification timer\) on a per odu-id basis. When enabled, an O-RU controller that has subscribed to the supervisionnotification is expected to configure one of the odu-id values in the supervision-watchdog-reset rpc. Operation of watchdog supervision timers on a per o-du basis does not obviate the O-RU from performing autonomous reset according to the scenario described in case \#2 above.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling

text: NOTE: The format of the odu-id string is not defined and not interpreted by the shared O-RU.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling

text: Case \#3: If the supervision timer associated with an odu-id expires, the O-RU shall set the state leaf of the following array carriers to DISABLED and the active leaf of the same carriers to INACTIVE:
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling

text:
* Any tx-array-carriers list entry including a list of odu-ids containing only expired odu-id.
  * Any rx-array-carriers list entry including a list of odu-ids containing only expired odu-id.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling

text: O-RU shall raise an alarm. The specific alarm \#35 "Lost O-DU ID based Supervision " is described in clause A. The O-RU sends tx-array-carriers-state-change and rx-array-carriers-state-change notifications to any notification subscribers. O-RU shall not perform an autonomous reset unless the requirements described in case \#2 are met.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.1 Supervision failure handling

text: 14.1.2 Supervision termination handling
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.2 Supervision termination handling

text: If NETCONF session used for the supervision subscription is terminated by NETCONF client, the O-RU disables operation of the watchdog timers for terminated NETCONF session and starts performing Call Home procedure towards call home O-RU Controllers, following specification in clause 6.3.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.2 Supervision termination handling

text: Before terminating its NETCONF session, a NETCONF client that has subscribed to receive supervision notification, should at least de-activate all carriers previously configured by this NETCONF client. Optionally, such a NETCONF client can also remove \(full or partial\) configuration applied by this NETCONF client to the O-RU.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.2 Supervision termination handling

text: If the per-odu-monitoring container is not present in the O-RU's configuration, in case when entering Supervision Termination handling, if the O-RU does not have running NETCONF session with any NETCONF client that has subscribed to receive the supervision-notification, the O-RU ceases all radio transmission.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.1.2 Supervision termination handling

text: If the per-odu-monitoring container is present in the O-RU's configuration, in case when entering Supervision Termination handling, the O-RU deactivates the array carriers associated with the odu-id value in its supervisionwatchdog-reset rpc as specified in clause 14.1.1.

text: 14.2 Log management
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2 Log management

text: 14.2.1 Introduction
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.1 Introduction

text: There are three type of log managements, troubleshooting log, security log and trace log. They are independent each other.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.1 Introduction

text: Troubleshooting log file contains the logs continuously collected before <start-troubleshooting-logs> rpc. Any logs collected after <start-troubleshooting-logs> rpc are not contained.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.1 Introduction

text: Trace log file contains the logs continuously collected after <start-trace-logs> rpc. Any logs collected before <starttrace-logs> rpc are not contained.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.1 Introduction

text: Security log files contain logs of security event information. The creation and storage of security log-data by the O-RU shall always be possible, i.e., there is no O-RAN defined procedure for starting or stopping the logging of security events. An O-RU indicates it supports O-RAN defined security logging procedures by including the SECURITY-LOGGING feature in its YANG library.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.1 Introduction

text: 14.2.2 Troubleshooting log management
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.2 Troubleshooting log management

text: By requesting trouble shooting log files an O-RU controller is able to obtain collected log data files that can be used for troubleshooting purposes.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.2 Troubleshooting log management

text: The O-RU can provide all possible troubleshooting log files. The contents and log formats are dependent on O-RU implementation.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.2 Troubleshooting log management

text: The number and size of files provided by O-RU is not restricted but the O-RU may keep the number and size of files reasonably small to allow completion of the whole "Troubleshooting data upload" scenario \(all files\) within 15 minutes \(with target to complete within 3 minutes\) - assuming no additional upload restrictions from connectivity bandwidth or file server implementation. It is also recommended to provide more useful files first.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.2 Troubleshooting log management

text: NOTE 1: The detailed O-RU controller behaviour is not specified. An O-RU controller can continue the scenario till completion past the allowed time or skip requesting further files
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.2 Troubleshooting log management

text: The files should be compressed with compression method indicated by file name extension:
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.2 Troubleshooting log management

text:
* .gz \(DEFLATE\),
  * .lz4 \(LZ4\),
  * .xz \(LZMA2 xz utils\),
  * .zip \(DEFLATE zlib library\).
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.2 Troubleshooting log management

text: O-RU shall collect log information. The RPC <start-troubleshooting-logs> shall trigger the O-RU to start generating troubleshooting log files containing troubleshooting logs, as illustrated in Figure 14.2.2-1. Completed generation of files shall be indicated by NETCONF server to NETCONF client in form of a notification.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.2 Troubleshooting log management

text: If an O-RU reports support for the LOG-FILTER feature, then the O-RU Controller may request selected troubleshooting log data to be generated by providing values in the filter list in the RPC <start-troubleshooting-logs>. In Troubleshooting Data Upload procedure NETCONF Server provides data, which match the provided filters in the filter list.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.2 Troubleshooting log management

text: NOTE 2: If the filter-type/value provided in the filter list is not supported by the O-RU, the O-RU can either ignore the filter-type/value, or reply with a status of FAILURE that indicates the failure reason being the non-support of the filter-type/value.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.2 Troubleshooting log management

text: The notification <troubleshooting-log-generated> shall be signalled to the notification subscriber after the O-RU has finished generation of all troubleshooting log files, indicating to the subscriber that the troubleshooting log files are ready to be uploaded.

text: 14.2.3 Security logs
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.3 Security logs

text: 14.2.3.1 Security log format
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.3.1 Security log format

text: An O-RU supporting the SECURITY-LOGGING feature shall ensure that the fields of individual security logs comply with the security log field requirements as specified in clause 5.3.8.8 of O-RAN Security Requirements Specifications \[83\]. The security logging by such an O-RU shall include the events mapped to an O-RAN Network Function in table 5.3.8.11.1-1 of \[83\].
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.3.1 Security log format

text: 14.2.3.2 Security log management
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.3.2 Security log management

text: There is no defined procedure for starting or stopping the logging of security events. The security log data shall be integrity protected and persistently stored in a non-volatile memory.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.3.2 Security log management

text: An O-RU supporting the SECURITY-LOGGING feature shall support the configuration of log-data rotation functionality. Log-rotation refers to closing a first log file and opening a second new log file. A log file can be closed based on a configured time interval, using the security-log-max-duration leaf, and/or a configured maximum size, using the security-log-max-size leaf. An O-RU may expose read-only data pertaining to the maximum size of the security log storage media using the leaf security-folder-memory-size.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.3.2 Security log management

text: The O-RU controller should configure log rotation parameters such that the size of a security log file does not exceed the maximum storage available in the O-RU.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.3.2 Security log management

text: NOTE 1: How the O-RU Controller uses the value of security-folder-memory-size and/or other available information to determine the log rotation parameters is out of scope of the present document.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.3.2 Security log management

text: The O-RU controller can arbitrarily decide to trigger the rotation of the current security log by sending the rotatesecurity-log rpc to the O-RU. An O-RU receiving the rotate-security-log rpc shall close the current security log file and open a new security log file.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.3.2 Security log management

text: When a log file is rotated, the preserved integrity protected log file should be stored. The O-RU shall store the security log files in the o-ran/security/ folder in O-RU.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.3.2 Security log management

text: NOTE 2: The details of the process used for file integrity protection is out of scope of the present document. The use by an O-RU of an encrypted file systems and/or encrypted folders to protect security logging data at rest are out of scope of the present document.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.3.2 Security log management

text: The filename name for security logs shall be of the format:
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.3.2 Security log management

text: S<start-time>\_<end-time>\_<name>.<ext>
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.3.2 Security log management

text:
* Starting with a capital letter "S".
  * Format of <start-time> and <end-time> can be local time or UTC.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.3.2 Security log management

text: Local time format is YYYYMMDDHHMM+HHMM, indicating, year, month, day, hour, minute, timezone "+" or "-" , hour and minute for the time zone.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.3.2 Security log management

text: UTC format is YYYYMMDDHHMMZ, indicating, year, month, day, hour, minute and with a special UTC designator \("Z"\)
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.3.2 Security log management

text: Time zone offset is provided by timezone-utc-offset in o-ran-operation.yang.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.3.2 Security log management

text:
* <name> in ietf-hardware is used.
  * "\_" underscore is located between <start-time>, <end-time> and <name>.
  * <ext> being the file extension. The extension shall indicate the archiving/encryption/compression method.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.2.3.2 Security log management

text: The O-RU Controller shall configure one or more remote-security-log-upload-path and associated credential information in the O-RU. text: 14.3 Trace
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.3 Trace

text: By requesting trace log files an O-RU controller is able to get them. Those trace log files contain collected log data files that can be used for trace purposes.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.3 Trace

text: The O-RU can provide all possible trace log files. The contents and log formats are dependent on O-RU implementation.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.3 Trace

text: The files should be compressed with compression method indicated by file name extension.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.3 Trace

text: O-RU shall start collecting the trace logs at the moment of receiving <start-trace-logs> rpc. Notification <trace-loggenerated> shall be periodically sent to O-RU controller whenever generated trace log files is\(are\) ready. File names of newly created log file\(s\) shall be included in notification. The number and size of files provided by O-RU in a single <trace-log-generated> notification is not restricted but the O-RU may keep the number and size of files reasonably small to allow completion of the whole "Trace data upload" scenario \(all files from notification\) within 15 minutes \(with target to complete within 3 minutes\) - assuming no additional upload restrictions from connectivity bandwidth or file server implementation.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.3 Trace

text: NOTE 1: Timing of creating new group of trace log files is up to O-RU implementation.
trace: 14.1 Supervision failure handling and supervision termination handling --> 14.3 Trace

text: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices

text: 14.4.1 Introduction
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.1 Introduction

text: An O-RU can connect to one or more external equipment including antenna line devices such as a RET, MultiRET, MHA, RAE and etc.
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.1 Introduction

text:
* For the communication with antenna line devices, AISG 2.0 protocol \[26\] as Layer 7 application and HDLC protocol as Layer 2 data link are used.
  * HDLC protocol as specified in ISO/IEC 13239 \[65\]. Detailed information can also be found in 3GPP TS 37.462 \[27\].
  * AISG 2.0 protocol is standardised by "Control interface for antenna line devices Standard No. AISG v2.0" \[26\] which is an adaptation of Iuant interface application layer defined in 3GPP TS 37.466 \[28\].
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.1 Introduction

text: An O-RU may provide one or more ALD ports supporting connection with Antenna Line Devices. Each ALD port shall be able to support more than one ALD \(i.e. a chained ALD configuration\).
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.1 Introduction

text: Through the model O-RU may optionally inform about hardware relation between ALD port and O-RU connector\(s\) used by specific ALD port. In case more than one O-RU connector is used by single ALD port, O-RU may extend "overcurrent-report" notification by adding exact list of O-RU connectors for which overcurrent condition is detected.
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.1 Introduction

text: This clause describes the communication mechanisms based on AISG 2.0 protocol as specified in AISG 2.0 \[26\]. For communication with external equipment, AISG 2.0 uses Application Part protocols \(RETAP, TMAAP etc.\) at Layer 7 and HDLC as a Layer 2 datalink protocol.
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.1 Introduction

text: 14.4.2 HDLC interworking
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.2 HDLC interworking

text: HDLC protocol is standardised by ISO/IEC 13239 \[65\]. Detailed information can also be found in 3GPP TS 37.462 \[27\].
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.2 HDLC interworking

text: NOTE: The assumed HDLC communication speed is 9 600 bits per second.
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.2 HDLC interworking

text: In order to handle collision detection in the HDLC branch, an O-RU supporting the ALD functionality shall support the following running counters reported using the corresponding YANG model:
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.2 HDLC interworking

text:
* Frames with wrong FCS
  * Frames without stop flag
  * Number of received octets
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.2 HDLC interworking

text: For running counters served by the O-RU, both the O-RU and NETCONF Client shall handle wrap-over mechanism in a way, that wrap over zero is not considered as erroneous situation.
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.2 HDLC interworking

text: A NETCONF client can recover these counters. From the changes observed in above counters, a NETCONF Client can deduce the presence of a collision on the HDLC bus. Additional diagnostic information may be derived from how these counters are incrementing.
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.2 HDLC interworking

text: Additionally, the O-RU implements "RPC Status" to indicate status of last "ald-communication" RPC to requestor.
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.2 HDLC interworking

text: • Status - flow control indicator of last requested operation \(Status of RPC\).
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.2 HDLC interworking

text: Prior to any communication with ALD\(s\), the O-RU shall provide ALDs with DC power. The way of how DC power is managed is out of scope of this interface specification.

text: 14.4.3 ALD operations

text: Figure 14.4.3-1 illustrates the ALD transfer procedure.
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.3 ALD operations

text:
* 1\) The NETCONF Client sends RPC <ald-communication> to the O-RU. The RPC has following input parameters: 
    * leaf: port-id \(uint8\) contains the identity of the ALD port. The O-RU shall output the data to \(corresponds to O-RU resources provided to NETCONF Client as inventory information\).
    * leaf: ald-req-msg \(up to 1 200 bytes\) may contain HDLC address, control bits and payload \(see: 3GPP TS 37.462 for details\).
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.3 ALD operations

text: The O-RU shall perform HDLC communication with the ALD as specified in \[27\] clause 4.5 "Message timing".
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.3 ALD operations

text:
* 2\) Immediately after the requested payload is sent to the ALD over the desired ALD port, the O-RU switches the ALD port into reception mode.
  * 3\) Bits received within reception window are formed to octets and inserted as payload into ald-resp-msg.
  * 4\) The O-RU responds to the NETCONF Client using the reply> message containing following parameters: 
    * leaf: port-id \(uint8\)
    * leaf: status
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.3 ALD operations

text:
* leaf: ald-resp-msg \(up to 1 200 bytes\)
  * leaf: frames-with-wrong-crc \(4 bytes\)
  * leaf: frames-without-stop-flag \(4 bytes\)
  * leaf: number-of-received-octets \(4 bytes\)
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.3 ALD operations

text: In case there is no response from the ALD received within the reception window, the record "ald-resp-msg" in <rpc-reply> sent by the O-RU shall be empty.
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.3 ALD operations

text: 5\) After reception, the O-RU shall wait a minimum of 3ms before the next transmission as per 3GPP TS 37.462, clause 4.5 "Message timing".

text: Precondition:
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.4.3 ALD operations --> Precondition:

text: M-Plane connectivity between NETCONF Client and NETCONF Server is successfully established. NETCONF Server reports presence of the supported HDLC Primary Devices.

* 1\) NETCONF Client triggers DC voltage on desired ALD ports using NETCONF <edit-config> RPC. After DC is turned on - NETCONF Client shall wait at least 3 s.
  * 2\) NETCONF Client performs HDLC bus scan using desired HDLC Primary Device offered by O-RU.
  * 3\) NETCONF Client determines presence of HDLC Secondary Devices connected to the ALD port.

text: 14.5 Operational aspects of external IO
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.5 Operational aspects of external IO

text: 14.5.1 Introduction
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.5.1 Introduction

text: An O-RU can connect to one or more input and output ports for external device supervision and control.
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.5.1 Introduction

text: The External IO has the following functions:
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.5.1 Introduction

text:
* INPUT: Supervising external devices.
  * OUTPUT: Controlling external devices.
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.5.1 Introduction

text: Also, external IO function includes signalling to get the O-RU and O-RU controller in sync, enables port monitoring on the O-RU and provides notification from the O-RU to an O-RU controller, and provides control from an O-RU controller to the O-RU and enables output port controlling on the O-RU.
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.5.1 Introduction

text: The O-RU only implements external IO yang module if the O-RU supports External IO aspect.
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.5.1 Introduction

text: Through the model O-RU may optionally inform about hardware relation between External IO and O-RU connector\(s\) used by specific External IO. Separate O-RU connectors may be reported for single External IO.
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.5.1 Introduction

text: A change in condition of the external IO shall not affect other O-RU services such as RF transmission / reception behaviour.
trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.5.1 Introduction

trace: 14.4 Operational aspects of antenna line devices --> 14.5.2 External input

  * 2\) To send notification from the O-RU to O-RU controller when input state is changed.

text: 15.2.1 Introduction
trace: 15.2 User plane message routing --> 15.2.1 Introduction

text: The purpose of U-Plane configuration is to define the relationship between U-Plane application endpoints in the O-DU and those in the O-RU. After such relationships are defined, the application endpoints are able to exchange IQ data using the U-Plane application protocol defined in clause 5.4 of \[2\].
trace: 15.2 User plane message routing --> 15.2.1 Introduction

text: Precondition:
trace: 15.2 User plane message routing --> 15.2.1 Introduction --> Precondition:

text: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID
trace: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID

text: The eAxC\_ID is used by C/U-plane application to manage eCPRI communication between desired C/U-Plane application components in O-DU and O-RU.
trace: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID

text: As defined in clause 5.1.3.2.7 of \[2\], the eAxC\_ID consists of four parameters: DU\_Port\_ID, RU\_Port\_ID, CC\_ID and BandSector\_ID. Order of parameters in eAxC\_ID shall follow definitions in CUS-Plane spec. In this version of the O-RAN WG4 specification, the length of eAxC\_ID is constant and equal to 16 bits. To enable optimal sharing of the 16 bits between these four parameters, the assignment of eAxC\_ID bits to parameters is not fixed. As a consequence, there is a need for NETCONF client to configure the bit assignment to parameters mappings using the M-Plane interface.
trace: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID

text: NOTE 1: \[2\] refers to the eAxC\_ID parameters as DU\_Port\_ID, RU\_Port\_ID, CC\_ID and BandSector\_ID and the present document and associated YANG models refer to the eaxc-id parameters as du-ports, ru-ports, ccids and band-sectors.
trace: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID

text: To handle flexible bit assignment, configurable bitmasks are defined for each parameter.
trace: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID

text: NOTE 2: Flexible configuration means, that bits of eAxC\_ID can be assigned to parameters in runtime.
trace: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID

text: Rules to be followed by NETCONF Client when configuring bit assignments:
trace: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID

text:
* notation used for parameters forming eAxC\_ID is from the LSB.
  * each parameter uses consecutive bits.
trace: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID
15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID
15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID
15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID
15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID

text:
* each parameter can occupy 0-16 bits.
  * single bit of eAxC\_ID cannot be assigned to more than one parameter.
trace: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID

text: RPC edit-config shall be used to configure bit assignments to O-RU.
trace: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID

text: Bit assignment change for parameters related to an existing carrier is not allowed. \(Impacted carriers need to be deactivated and deleted prior to any change in eAxC\_ID configuration, and then be subsequently created and activated.\)
trace: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID

text: 15.2.3 U-Plane endpoint addressing
trace: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID --> 15.2.3 U-Plane endpoint addressing

text: Parameter "eaxc-id" for low-level-tx-endpoint and low-level-rx-endpoint, defined using an unsigned 16-bit integer, shall follow the eaxc-id addressing schema defined in clause 15.2.2. Refer to the eaxc-id parameter description in CUS plane specification clause 5.1.3.2.7 of \[2\].
trace: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID --> 15.2.3 U-Plane endpoint addressing

text: The NETCONF Client shall assign unique values to the "eaxc\_id" addresses to all low-level-rx-endpoint elements and low-level-tx-endpoint elements, within the O-RU when operating in the same direction \(Tx or Rx\), even when these operate across different named interfaces of the O-RU.
trace: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID --> 15.2.3 U-Plane endpoint addressing

text: More precisely, the same eaxc-id cannot be simultaneously assigned to multiple low-level-rx-endpoints or to multiple and low-level-tx-endpoints. Clarifying eaxc-id assignment by example, and unless otherwise specified, within the same O-RU \(considering a 2 × 2 MIMO\):
trace: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID --> 15.2.3 U-Plane endpoint addressing

text: Case 1: Allowed eaxc-id assignment \(same antenna ports used for Tx and Rx\)
trace: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID --> 15.2.3 U-Plane endpoint addressing

text:
* low-level-rx-endpoint \(name 1\) eaxc-id=1
  * low-level-tx-endpoint \(name 1\) eaxc-id=1
  * low-level-rx-endpoint \(name 2\) eaxc-id=2
  * low-level-tx-endpoint \(name 2\) eaxc-id=2
trace: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID --> 15.2.3 U-Plane endpoint addressing

text: Case 2: Allowed eaxc-id assignment \(separate antenna ports used for Tx and Rx\)
trace: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID --> 15.2.3 U-Plane endpoint addressing

text:
* low-level-rx-endpoint \(name 1\) eaxc-id=1
  * low-level-tx-endpoint \(name 1\) eaxc-id=2
  * low-level-rx-endpoint \(name 2\) eaxc-id=3
  * low-level-tx-endpoint \(name 2\) eaxc-id=4
trace: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID --> 15.2.3 U-Plane endpoint addressing

text: Case 3: Prohibited eaxc-id assignment \(separate antenna ports used for Tx and Rx\)
trace: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID --> 15.2.3 U-Plane endpoint addressing

text:
* low-level-rx-endpoint \(name 1\) eaxc-id=1
  * low-level-tx-endpoint \(name 1\) eaxc-id=2
  * low-level-rx-endpoint \(name 2\) eaxc-id=1
  * low-level-tx-endpoint \(name 2\) eaxc-id=2
trace: 15.2.2 Configurable format for eAxC\_ID --> 15.2.3 U-Plane endpoint addressing
